questions.prompt: Believe me, judges, the accused man will flee before dawn.
questions.answer: Crēdite mihi, jūdicēs, reus ante aurōram fugiet.

questions.prompt: O son, alone the source of my great power, do not fear.
questions.answer: Nāte, mea magna potentia sōlus, nōlī timēre.

questions.prompt: Listen, soldiers, to the general who leads you to victory.
questions.answer: Audīte, mīlitēs, ducem quī vōs ad victōriam dūcit.

questions.prompt: Come here, faithful friend, and share these feasts with me.
questions.answer: Venī hūc, amīce fidēlis, et hās epulās mēcum partīre.

questions.prompt: Hear ye, Alban people, the words of your king!
questions.answer: Audī tū, populus Albānus, verba rēgis tuī!

questions.prompt: Spare the conquered, brave victor, when the battle is over.
questions.answer: Parce victīs, victor magnanime, cōnfectō proeliō.

questions.prompt: Why do you weep, wretched mother, mourning your slain son?
questions.answer: Cūr flēs, māter misera, fīlium tuum occīsum lūgēns?

questions.prompt: Do not despair, citizens, though the enemy presses at the gates.
questions.answer: Nōlīte dēspērāre, cīvēs, quamquam inimīcus portīs īnstat.

questions.prompt: Sing, O Muse, of the man renowned for his cunning.
questions.answer: Cane, ō Mūsa, virum astūtiā clārum.

questions.prompt: Forgive me, gentle father, for I have erred greatly.
questions.answer: Ignōsce mihi, mītis pater, nam graviter errāvī.

questions.prompt: You, notorious traitor, will pay the penalty for your crime.
questions.answer: Tū, prōditor īnfāmis, poenās sceleris tuī dabis.

questions.prompt: Rejoice, young men, while fortune smiles upon your endeavors.
questions.answer: Gaudēte, juvenēs, dum fortūna cōnātibus vestrīs arrīdet.

questions.prompt: Beware, careless traveler, the paths hidden by darkness.
questions.answer: Cavē, viātor incaute, viās tenebrīs occultās.

questions.prompt: O gods, protect the city besieged by cruel foes.
questions.answer: Ō dī, urbem ab hostibus crūdēlibus obsessam servāte.

questions.prompt: Speak the truth, boy, lest you increase our fear.
questions.answer: Vērum dīc, puer, nē timōrem nostrum augeās.

questions.prompt: Remember me, dear comrades, when you return to your homeland.
questions.answer: Mementōte meī, sociī cārī, cum in patriam redieritis.

questions.prompt: O king, magnificent in war, grant peace to the suppliants.
questions.answer: Ō rēx, bellō magnifice, pācem supplicibus concēde.

questions.prompt: Trust the gods, wise old man, who guide all things.
questions.answer: Crēde deīs, senex sapiēns, quī omnia regunt.

questions.prompt: Endure these hardships, comrade, for a better day will come.
questions.answer: Fer haec dūra, comes, nam melior diēs veniet.

questions.prompt: Approach without fear, stranger, and tell us your name.
questions.answer: Accēde sine metū, hospes, et nōbīs nōmen tuum dīc.

questions.prompt: O queen, most beautiful of women, why do you grieve?
questions.answer: Ō rēgīna, fēminārum pulcherrima, cūr maerēs?

questions.prompt: Follow me, brave companions, into the thick of battle.
questions.answer: Sequiminī mē, fortēs comitēs, in mediam pugnam.

questions.prompt: O immortal gods, where in the world are we, what commonwealth do we have, in what city do we live?
questions.answer: Ō dī immortālēs, ubinam gentium sumus? Quam rem pūblicam habēmus? In quā urbe vīvimus?

questions.prompt: O immortal gods, where in the world are we?
questions.answer: Ō dī immortālēs, ubinam gentium sumus?

questions.prompt: But this man, about whom I myself now say so much — oh, immortal gods, what is it, what does it avail?
questions.answer: Hic vērō, dē quō ego ipse tam multa nunc dīcō. Prō, dī immortālēs! Quid est? Quid valet?

questions.prompt: Do so, my Lucilius: lay claim to yourself for yourself, and gather and keep the time which until now was being taken from you, or stolen, or slipping away.
questions.answer: Ita fac, mī Lūcīlī: vindicā tē tibi, et tempus quod adhūc aut auferēbātur aut subripiēbātur aut excidēbat collige et servā.

questions.prompt: They say, finally, that he was so distraught that for months on end, with beard and hair let grow, he would sometimes dash his head against the doors, crying out: 'Quintilius Varus, give me back my legions!'.
questions.answer: Adeō dēnique cōnsternātum ferunt ut, per continuōs mēnsēs barbā capillōque summissō, caput interdum foribus illīderet, vōciferāns: “Quīntilī Vāre, legiōnēs redde!”

questions.prompt: O father Tiber, thee, holy one, I pray.
questions.answer: Tiberīne pater, tē, sāncte, precor.

questions.prompt: My whole attention will be devoted to you, Hortensius.
questions.answer: Rēs omnis mihi tēcum erit, Hortēnsī.

questions.prompt: Hear, you people of Alba.
questions.answer: Audī tū, populus Albānus.

questions.prompt: I should bid you go on and prosper in your valor.
questions.answer: Iubērem tē macte virtūte esse.

questions.prompt: In heaven’s name, how long, Catiline, wilt trifle with our patience?
questions.answer: quō usque tandem abūtēre, Catilīna, patientiā nostrā?

questions.prompt: Good bye, my absent loves, good bye.
questions.answer: valēte, dēsīderia mea, valēte.

questions.prompt: Stick to town, dear Rufus, yes, to town.
questions.answer: urbem, urbem, mī Rūfe, cole.
